Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed pattern: sharp increase in request queuing on the US-W2 host pool starting at 08:42 PDT. CPU and memory on instances are normal; however, internal request queue length (per-worker) jumped 6x and kernel scheduling wait increased.
- Error surface: majority of 5xx are 502/503 Gateway/Upstream errors coming from our local routing layer when requests timeout waiting for model worker availability.
- Correlation: a routing config change rolled out at 08:30 that adjusted shard affinity for a small subset of customers (A/B routing experiment). Telemetry shows the new affinity caused hot-spotting in a narrow set of hosts in US-W2, exhausting the in-memory KV cache and causing repeated cold-starts for some model variants.

Immediate mitigations performed (10:00–10:03):
1) Reverted the affinity tweak (rolled back the 08:30 config) — reduced new request skew back to baseline.
2) Increased worker concurrency on US-W2 pool by +15% (hotfix) to relieve queue pressure.
3) Started a controlled 25% diversion of SkyMotion traffic to US-East-2 (us-east-2) using feature-routing (canary).

Observables (10:04): 5xx rate dropped from 7.4% to 2.1%; median latency trending down from 650ms toward ~210ms. Queue depth charts attached for reference.

Proposed next steps (recommendation):
- Expand diversion to 40% for next 30 minutes while we monitor.
- Warm additional model workers in US-East-2 to absorb persistent load and pre-populate KV caches.
- Post-mortem: revert A/B experiment until we have auto-sharding to prevent hot-spotting.
